relationships.description: Actors holding the role are able to read or modify the protected resource, by virtue of the role's permissions naming operations on that resource.
relationships.evidence: The role's policy or RBAC definition (e.g. a Kubernetes RoleBinding rule, IAM policy, or Casbin policy line) lists the resource's identifier as an object it may act on.

relationships.description: The role bundles the permission as one of its member grants, while the permission remains an independent definition that other roles may also include.
relationships.evidence: The role definition file or role_permissions join table lists the permission's identifier among the role's grants, and the same permission appears under other roles.

relationships.description: Being assigned the role is what entitles an actor to exercise the permission at enforcement points, so authorization checks for that permission succeed for role holders.
relationships.evidence: An authorization check such as hasPermission or @PreAuthorize resolves the permission by looking up the caller's roles, and the role's mapping includes that permission.

relationships.description: The role is one of the conflicting positions named by the separation-of-duty rule, so its assignment or use is restricted relative to the other role or task in the conflicting pair.
relationships.evidence: An SoD policy or mutual-exclusion constraint in the IAM configuration names the role as conflicting with another role or workflow step, and role-assignment or approval code rejects violations.

relationships.description: The technical access role corresponds to the organizational responsibility position, granting system access to whoever fills that business role.
relationships.evidence: An access-provisioning matrix, identity-governance mapping, or directory group naming convention ties the security role to the business role (e.g. 'Claims Adjuster' group grants the CLAIMS_ADJUSTER role).

relationships.description: The role makes the permission available to every actor assigned to it, so actors gain the grant through the role rather than individually.
relationships.evidence: The role-to-permission mapping in the RBAC configuration is used by the user-permission resolver to compute an actor's effective permissions from their assigned roles.

relationships.description: The child role is a more specific variant of its parent role, inheriting all of the parent's permissions and adding its own, typically at a higher privilege tier.
relationships.evidence: The role definition declares a parent or inherits attribute (e.g. a role hierarchy entry 'admin inherits editor') and permission resolution unions in the parent's permissions.

notes: aggregates, authorizes and provides from Role to Permission all express the same role-grants-permission membership; one (aggregates) suffices. Role accesses SecureResource is derivable via Permission and is redundant. specializes duplicates single-parent inheritance correctly but should be restricted to one parent.
